HISTORY & PHYSICAL (DETAILED) NOTE

Consult Summary:
40-year-old woman with 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and mild hematuria—treated empirically as an acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “It hurts when I pee.”  
• Onset & course: Began 6 days ago; symptoms persist.  
• Character: Burning/pain on micturition; foul-smelling urine.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent lower-mid abdominal (suprapubic) pain rated 7/10, spots of blood in urine.  
• Denies: Fever, chills, flank/loin/back pain, nausea/vomiting, vaginal discharge, change in bowel habit, weight loss, prior similar episodes.  
• Triggers/relievers: Not identified.  
• Hydration & intake: Eating and drinking normally.  
• Gynecologic: Regular periods.  
• Sexual/urinary history: No recent sexual activity or other precipitating factors reported.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) – no recent exacerbation described.  
• No history of kidney disease or previous urinary infections.  
• No surgeries reported.

Medications:
• Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily (regular).  
• Antibiotic for UTI (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) – prescription to be collected.  

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – reaction not specified.

Social History:
• Lives with friends; occupation: support worker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine per week.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• No significant familial illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (remote video consult).  
• General / Abdominal / GU exam: Not performed (telemedicine).

Investigations:
• None obtained; no urinalysis or culture ordered at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis highly suspected based on classic symptom cluster without systemic or upper-tract features.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis – dysuria, foul odor, suprapubic pain, mild hematuria; no fever or flank pain.  
2. Urethritis (Chlamydia/Gonorrhoea) – dysuria/hematuria possible; less likely: no discharge, limited sexual risk history.  
3. Urinary tract calculi – intermittent pain and hematuria support; absence of colicky flank pain opposes.

Issue 1: Suspected acute uncomplicated lower UTI  
• Empiric 3-day oral antibiotic course (specific agent dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Encourage oral hydration 2.5–3 L/day.  
• Advice: cranberry juice and over-the-counter urinary alkalising sachets.  
• Obtain home thermometer; monitor temperature.  
• Safety-net: Seek review if pain worsens, develops fever, flank/back pain, urinary retention, or if symptoms persist/recur.  
• Follow-up: No routine review required if symptoms resolve; otherwise re-consult.

Issue 2: Irritable bowel syndrome – stable  
• Continue Mebeverine 200 mg TID.  
• No further action today.

Issue 3: Medication allergy documentation  
• Recorded allergy to clindamycin; ensure avoidance in future prescriptions.

General plan items:  
• Prescription sent to Knightsbridge Pharmacy; patient to collect within ~1 hour and start therapy today.  
• Provide written advice via electronic notes.

Quality checks:
● No vitals, physical exam, or urinalysis performed—expected but understandable in teleconsult; consider UA/culture if symptoms recur.  
● Antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency not documented.  
● Reaction details for clindamycin allergy not specified.  
● Transcript clear; no major conflicts between transcript and DDx noted.
